text:
Dear advisers,

When I signed my lease with Sonnbühl Property Ltd in autumn 2022, it set out a staircase of rent rises: CHF 60 more per month every year on 1 June, with all the amounts written down in advance. I've paid each step without complaint. The rise that is due this June is simply the next step on that list.

What I can't get over is that on 2 March 2026 I got two things in the same envelope from Mr Ian Egli: the notice of that rent step, and a notice terminating my lease on the flat at Wiesenstrasse 94 in Chur. The termination even says it is connected to the rent change. So in one go they put my rent up and threw me out.

To be precise about the rent: the form says that from 1 June 2026 I'm to pay CHF 2430 a month instead of CHF 2370. My friend Anna Wälti, who has a similar lease, says she has never heard of a landlord raising the rent and terminating at the same time, and that it looks like an attempt to push me into signing a new, more expensive contract.

I've attached the rent notice.

I've attached the termination too. I'd like to know whether I can fight the termination, and whether I have to pay the higher rent while that's being sorted out.

Thank you,
Nina Wyss
